nodeData.topic: Day 5 · Session 2 · Wrong worship and the darkest region
nodeData.note: Sri Isopanisad 12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Mantra 12 warns that worshipping demigods, or an impersonal absolute, also leads into darkness, because only Krishna, the fully independent person, can free us from birth and death. Maharaj contrasts the self-luminous spiritual world with the dark shell of the universe, and with the class discusses the moon missions, pseudo-religion and science taken as a faith. Questions follow on Lord Siva, Ravana, and praying to Sarasvati or Ganesa. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 5 · Session 1 · The dhira and balanced knowledge
nodeData.note: Sri Isopanisad 10–11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj finishes the purport's list of items of real knowledge — take only what you need, serve with rapt attention — and applies Mantra 10 to modern education, families, religious quarrels and the need to approach a truly undisturbed dhira. Mantra 11 calls for knowing both maya and Krishna: material problems have no material solution, so we practise sense control now and prepare to go back to Godhead. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Continuing the purport's eighteen items of real knowledge from the tenth: do not take more than you need, do not identify with the body, and serve Krishna with full attention.

Maharaj asks what quantity we need. It is not about body size — he has seen small people eat heavily and large people eat little — it depends on each person and the work they do.

Devotees who eat a lot in the temple often eat less after marriage, because outside they must work. Early devotees ate twice a day, went out on sankirtana and lived simply; that austerity and sincerity brought miracles. nodeData.note: Sri Isopanisad 7–8 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj finishes Mantra 7: the soul is meant for enjoyment, but only by serving Krishna, like a hand feeding the stomach, and prasada gives the higher taste that brings detachment. Mantra 8 describes the Lord's spiritual, fully independent form, any of whose senses can do anything, and his power to turn matter into spirit, so the installed deity is Krishna himself. nodeData.topic: Day 3 · Session 1 · The inconceivable, very near
nodeData.note: Sri Isopanisad 4–5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains Mantras 4 and 5: the Lord stays in his abode yet outruns the mind, is far away yet nearer than anyone, and is inconceivable except by his mercy. Along the way he shows how to answer someone claiming to be God, why even sages and demigods cannot know Krishna fully, how sincerity lets us recognise a pure devotee, and why deities are not idols. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.note: Sri Isopanisad 1–2 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj goes deeper into Mantra 1: everything moving and unmoving is Krishna's, greed disturbs others, and living by our quota would turn this world into Vaikuntha. nodeData.note: Sri Isopanisad Invocation and Mantra 1 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. nodeData.topic: Day 1 · Session 1 · Vedic knowledge, the complete whole
nodeData.note: Sri Isopanisad Introduction and Invocation · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens the Isopanisad unit of the Bhakti Shastri course: what the Vedas and Upanishads are, why Srila Prabhupada put Vishnu on the cover, and an overview of all eighteen mantras. He then explains the four defects of conditioned souls, why Vedic knowledge is received like a mother's word through disciplic succession, and leads the class in exploring how Krishna is complete. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
The host welcomes devotees to the last unit of the Bhakti Shastri course and introduces Maharaj: a seeker whose questions about karma and reincarnation went unanswered at school, who found the Hare Krishnas through a newspaper advertisement and later became the first African sannyasi to serve as an initiating guru.

Could you…”

Maharaj begins humbly: he has not come to teach but to learn from the class, and counts it his fortune to be among them. — “I'm not a teacher. I only came here to learn from all of you.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:20 (auto-transcript): “I'm not a teacher. I only came here to learn from all of you. I don't expect I'm going to teach you. It is my fortune to have a mission from all of you in this class. Perfect example. yeah perfect example i don't expect to see you here i'm just surprised and i saw you perfect…”

Over the coming days the class will go through the eighteen mantras. Maharaj starts with the place of the Upanishads within the Vedas.

The Vedas are called sruti because they were heard, not studied from paper as we do now. People remembered what they heard; there were four Vedas — Rig, Sama, Yajur and Atharva. — “their head was their recorder.”

children.note:
The word Isa points to the supreme controller. Srila Prabhupada insisted that a painting of Vishnu, not Krishna, go on the cover of the book.

Throughout his explanations Prabhupada speaks of Vishnu rather than Krishna, because the Upanishads start from an impersonal platform and lead the reader step by step toward the personal Lord.

Maharaj traces the Upanishad's history through Svayambhuva Manu, his wife Satarupa and their children. From the line of his daughter Akuti comes Yajna, an incarnation of Vishnu — another reason the Vishnu form is used.

children.note:

children.topic: The aim is to find Krishna
children.note:
The goal of Vedic study is not speculation but finding Krishna. Maharaj outlines the Vedic literature — the four Vedas, the Mahabharata and Puranas, the Vedanta-sutra and its natural commentary, the Bhagavatam — and says this movement is fully authorised by it.

The Truth is complete only as all three features together. Brahman alone or Paramatma alone leaves something missing; Bhagavan, full in eternity, knowledge and bliss, is the complete picture.
